calibration_rulings.title: kanzan-park's title: both source titles carry a SECOND NAME in a bracket ('Kanzan Adventure Park (Al-Shu'bah)'); the stage checker reports a bracket in a title as a gloss in a heading.
calibration_rulings.binds: kanzan-park::title; the termbase key of the page (it carries the bracket).
calibration_rulings.ruling: A — THE TITLE KEEPS THE BRACKET BOTH SOURCE TITLES CARRY: «جبل کنزان کی تفریح گاہ (الشعبہ)». This is a new case, not a reopening: a bracket that holds a second NAME which BOTH source titles carry in a bracket is not a gloss; it stands at the end of the title, holds the name as its termbase key and nothing else, and is the only kind of bracket a title may carry. The gloss rules stand untouched for what they were made for: no gloss, no Urdu generic and no bracket of any other kind in a title, a kicker, a label or a question, and no bracket directly after a jabal name (here the bracket follows the generic of the park). The title follows the Arabic name ('Mountain'; the English-only 'Adventure' is not written), on the approved key of the mountain. THE CHECKER'S FINDING IS CARRIED, not answered by reshaping the title: I hold that the probe reaches further than the rule it guards and I report it; I did not edit the tool. FALLBACK, named so that a later round does not have to find it: if the coordinator holds the two guards to their letter, or the probe is not taught the case, the title is D, «جبل کنزان / الشعبہ کی تفریح گاہ» — both names kept, the device of the page's own summary — with the cost the first reader showed on mushaqar's slash (the possessive attaches to the second name only); never B, which drops a name both sources carry. ROUND 2: A CONFIRMED, on its merits and on the second reader's evidence, and no longer carried as a finding. THE EXCEPTION IS WRITTEN WHERE THE GUARDS ARE: the two guards that bar a bracket in a title by their letter are carried in this file as entries P3a and P3c-labels, each with this item's exception in its guard, so that each ruling, its guard and its notes agree and stand alone. THE FALLBACK IS CORRECTED, on the proof pass's finding 11: D is WITHDRAWN (its possessive falls on the second name alone, here a village's key). If a title without a bracket is ever forced, it is the order of the page's own summary, «الشعبہ / جبل کنزان کی تفریح گاہ», which puts the possessive on the mountain and departs from the order of both source titles; B, which drops a name both sources carry, stays the last resort. The key in termbase_final is byte for byte the title. ‖ ENTERED ON APPLY (2026-10-14), proof pass on round 2, note 6: two rulings still restate the old letter "no bracket in a title" and are read under this exception: ruling A of N70 (a jabal name takes no bracket, in title or body; it binds pages whose source glosses the name, and defers to the guards of P3a and P3c as amended here), and b0-ui's own P3c-labels (round 3), which governs the interface strings, not the attraction batches. Neither binds kanzan-park's title; neither is reworded. ‖ AMENDED IN b14 (judge round 1, 2026-10-15; OWNER DECIDED 2026-10-15 (N119 reversed; DECISIONS «Owner's answers on 2026-10-15», «Batch b13-ui», «Batches b14 and b15»); item N202 A): The title is «جبل کنزان پارک (الشعبہ)» (item N199 B, masculine): the bracket follows the park's generic «پارک», closes the title and holds the second name alone; the bracket rule is unchanged. The fallback, if a title without a bracket is ever forced, reads «الشعبہ / جبل کنزان پارک». The key in termbase_final is byte for byte the title.
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader, not machine-read: a title carries a bracket only where both source titles close with a second name in a bracket; the bracket holds that name and nothing else and closes the title, and the whole title is a termbase key, byte for byte. No bracket follows a jabal name directly. The stage checker's heading probe tests the same conditions since round 2 of b7.

calibration_rulings.title: The pattern of a park title with the owner's noun «پارک»: N101's possessive (A) or the compound name + «پارک» (B), for b14 and b15 at once.

Every later park page.
calibration_rulings.ruling: B — THE COMPOUND for every park whose title is named by a PROPER NAME (a place, a spring, a mountain, a person or family): the name as its termbase key, then «پارک», no possessive; masculine. b14: «الاحساء قومی پارک», «جواثا پارک», «عین النجم پارک», «المشقر پارک» (former name in its own clause: «جو پہلے الشیبانی پارک کہلاتا تھا»), «جبل کنزان پارک (الشعبہ)» with N103's bracket, the official name «“جبل الشعبہ پارک”» (N72), «الموسیٰ پارک» (N85, unchanged). b15: «شاہ عبد اللہ ماحولیاتی پارک» (N85, unchanged); a title whose head is a DESCRIPTION keeps the possessive: «کھیلوں کے اسٹیڈیم کا پارک» (N124). A garden stays «باغ» («الکوت کا باغ», N121). WHY: (1) Urdu names parks as compounds — person, neighbourhood, river, lake and Arabic article names alike (stage 4: «اقبال پارک» 117 / «اقبال کا پارک» 0; «جناح پارک» 128 / «جناح کا پارک» 0; «ماڈل ٹاؤن پارک», «چناب پارک», «الحسین عوامی پارک»), while «… کا پارک» is descriptive («جنگلی حیات کا پارک»); (2) N101 refused the compound because it was 'attested once with this generic' — a reason about «تفریح گاہ» that the owner's noun removes; N101 itself named A's cost, that the title 'reads as a description … rather than as what the place is called'; (3) one pattern on the leisure index instead of two, which the reader of this round noticed (item 35); (4) the jabal name takes a following generic as a compound («جبل علی بندرگاہ» 2 / «… کی بندرگاہ» 0), so D is refused; C is refused (stage 4). COST, named: the six names are unattested in Urdu in either form (stage 4: 0 each), so the choice is by the pattern, not by a count; for the national park alone A was attested too («دونانہ کا قومی پارک»), and the set is not split on it. The text changes in 13 leaves (changes 0–12), no agreement moves; the seven keys are entered in the compound (termbase_final) and the old keys retired. UNREAD: the proof pass and a fresh blind read on this round follow before apply. ‖ ROUND 2: CONFIRMED on the fresh reader and the proof. termbase_keys_retired lists the seven old keys of the termbase and the six possessive keys proposed at stages 1–4, which were never entered: the meta step retires only the first seven (proof on r1, note 7).
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader, not machine-read: a park title named by a proper name is the name as its termbase key, then «پارک», with no «کا» / «کی» / «کے» between them; a title whose head is a description (b15 stadium-park) keeps the possessive; every body or question mention of the page's name is the title's key byte for byte, inflected only by a following postposition («جواثا پارک میں»); agreeing forms masculine. The stage checker holds titles to their keys and reports a retired key (termbase_keys_retired below).

Round 1's rewording took the clause out of the machine reader altogether and did not 'scope it to its binds' as said: the guard reader has no scoping by binds, so no machine clause can bite on zaki-alsalem-farm only. N178's guard is now the whole-word clause «نخلستان کے مشرق» does not occur as a whole word: machine-read on every attraction page, it bites on the phrase 'east of the oasis' itself and not on «مشرقی» ('eastern'). Page scoping by binds, if wanted, is a tool change for the coordinator. N178's text is the termbase's, its owner question kept open.
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader, not machine-read: a guard clause meant for one page is worded so that its pattern cannot occur legitimately on another (here: a whole word).
